messages:
marco: spotting a slow-growth in pending GPUs in asia-east1-a — mostly small jobs but a couple of 16GPU backfills blocked

tess: what does `kubectl describe` say for a blocked pod?

anya: pending pod excerpt:
```
Name: heavy-train-09
Status: Pending (0/60 nodes fit: Insufficient contiguous gpus)
Annotations: redwood/reserve-owner: maintenance-2026-03
Resources: requests.nvidia.com/gpu: 16
```

marco: nodes report free capacity but many are labeled `reserve=maintenance` with reserve-ttl=72h; these are supposed to be soft reservations but scheduler treats them as hard anchors

infra-bot: [alert] fragment_alert asia-east1-a unusable_gpus=48 anomaly=0.71 triggered=1767333300

tess: last week we shipped the reserve-ttl feature (rollout r2026-03-reserve) which defaulted to 72h. ops accidentally used that label for long maintenance windows — TTL should have been 2h for soft reserves

anya: immediate mitigation: reduce reserve TTL on maintenance reservations to 2h and relax contiguous-slot enforcement for requests >=8 GPUs so big jobs can colocate where possible

ops-oncall: approved manual override. running: `kubectl label nodes -l reserve=maintenance reserve-ttl=2h --overwrite`

marco: after override some nodes show contiguous 16 free. scheduling events show two 16GPU pods bound. pending dropped from 7->3

tess: follow-up: add a sanity-check in the reserve label controller to block TTL >24h for non-critical families and emit audit warnings. create INFRA-8834

infra-bot: [note] INFRA-8834 created: reserve-ttl-safety-check assigned eng-infra

anya: also recommend a scheduled nightly defragment pass for clusters with >2% unusable GPUs for more than 30m — conservative move-first for small pods only

ops-oncall: good plan. monitoring will alert on unusable-gpu ratio and auto-open remediation run if threshold crossed

marco: closing thread — two large jobs scheduled. will watch for regression over next 2 hours. :white_check_mark:
